subject: App implementation bridge: SDK setup, endpoint migration & retry guidance
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex@pixeltail.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: App implementation & migration questions

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to start moving our main app from the existing vendor to Redwood's hosted endpoints next quarter. Before we kick off the implementation sprint, the engineering team asked for a short checklist and concrete guidance on these items: SDK initialization examples (Node + Python), recommended retry/backoff pattern for 429s and 5xxs, how to migrate from our current /v1/generate endpoint to Redwood's streaming endpoints without breaking client UX, and a simple rate-limit handling strategy that fits a mobile-first product.

Can you send sample code and a minimal migration playbook we can hand to our engineers? We want to scope the work (effort estimate) and identify any blockers early (IP, contract, or security items).

Thanks — Alex
Alex Ramos
Head of Integrations, Pixeltail AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex@pixeltail.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: App implementation & migration questions

Alex —

Great questions. I've attached a short implementation checklist and a sample retry config (YAML) that matches what we use in production. High level answers up front so your team can triage:  

- SDKs: we support official SDKs for Node and Python. Initialization is a single-line token plus optional timeout/retries config.
- Endpoint migration: treat the streaming endpoint as a backward-compatible upgrade; start by mirroring the same request body and enabling streaming on a canary route.
- Retries/timeouts: we recommend an exponential backoff with full jitter for 429/5xx, capped retries (3 for mobile-first sync flows, 5 for backend-to-backend).
- Rate limits: prefer client-side token bucket + server-side graceful 429 + Retry-After handling. For mobile, fall back to queued retry with progressive UX degradation (spinner -> reduced feature).

Marissa and Ben, can you add a couple of concrete snippets (Node/Python) and an example of a small client fallback UX we can share with Alex?

-J

--
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex@pixeltail.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: App implementation & migration questions

Alex —

Attached are the code snippets (also pasted below) and a short implementation sequence we recommend for a low-risk migration. I'll keep this intentionally minimal so engineers can copy/paste.

1) Minimal migration sequence (2-week canary):
   - Week 0: Create a canary routing rule for 5% of requests -> Redwood hosted endpoint. Mirror logging and latency metrics.
   - Week 1: Increase to 25% after smoke tests. Run automated E2E prompt tests for quality regression.
   - Week 2: Full cutover + rollback window (24h).

2) Node (official SDK) init and streaming example:

const Redwood = require('@redwoodai/sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, timeoutMs: 60000 });

(async () => {
  const stream = client.stream({ model: 'gpt-redwood-1', input: 'Summarize user query' });
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    // UI: append chunk to response area
    process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
  }
})();

Graceful fallback (non-streaming) for older clients:
try {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-redwood-1', input: '...' });
} catch (err) {
  // degrade to server-generated summary or cached response
}

3) Python init / retry wrapper (requests style SDK):

from redwood import Client
import time, random

client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'), timeout=60)

def request_with_retries(payload, max_retries=3):
    backoff = 0.5
    for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
        try:
            return client.generate(payload)
        except Exception as e:
            code = getattr(e, 'status_code', None)
            if code in (429, 503, 500):
                sleep = backoff * (2 ** attempt) * random.random()
                time.sleep(sleep)
                continue
            raise
    raise RuntimeError('Retries exhausted')

4) Recommended retry policy summary:
   - 429: exponential backoff with full jitter, cap 3 retries for mobile UI flows. Honor Retry-After header if present.
   - 5xx: backoff + incrementally shift to degraded feature set (server-side cache).
   - Circuit breaker: open after N consecutive 5xx (e.g., 6) for 60s, let health checks close it.

Let me know if you want these in a GitHub gist or included in an implementation ticket template.

-M

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

This is excellent, thank you. A couple quick clarifications from our engineers:  
- For streaming, does Redwood support partial response caching so we can show progressive UI even when a user drops connection mid-stream?
- If we set client-side token bucket limits, what headroom should we leave relative to the quota returned by your control plane to avoid hitting automatic throttles?

Also, sending over our SOC 2 intake contact (contracts@pixeltail.ai) — Monica, can you confirm any SAML/KMS requirements we should include in the security questionnaire?

Thanks — Alex
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex@pixeltail.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: App implementation & migration questions

Alex —

Quick answers:  
- Partial response caching: yes — our runtime supports incremental KV cache writes for streaming sessions. If a connection drops, you can resume from the last token using the session_id and cached KV. We'll include a short snippet in the Drive folder.
- Token bucket headroom: aim for ~20% headroom under the control-plane quota to smooth bursts; e.g., if quota=100 rps, set client_token_bucket to 80 rps with a 2s refill quantum. That keeps you below automatic throttles while still allowing short bursts.
- Monica: for SOC2 intake, the common asks are SAML SSO, KMS integration (customer-managed keys supported in Private tier), and audit log exports. Monica, can you send a short one-pager for Alex's contracts team?

I've uploaded the checklist, sample_retry_config.yaml, and a small snippets text file to the migration folder here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-migration-kit — sharing permissions set to viewer for your domain.

Next steps we propose:
- I’ll open a 2-week canary implementation ticket and add sample test prompts (owner: Marissa).
- Alex: confirm scope and any legal/SOC asks we should pre-clear.

If that works, we’ll schedule a 30-minute engineering walkthrough next Tuesday.

Thanks — J

--
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
